summary: Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and held posts at Ryukoku University and Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Senta, both attested in 2003.
Yoshitoyo Ohara works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshihito Muroji is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (until 1992) under Lambert Schmithausen, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. His career includes posts at Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Shiga University of Medical Science.
Yoshiko Shimabukuro focused on Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at Kyoto Chuo Bukkyo Gakuen through 1936 and subsequently attended Kyoto Women's University from 1936 to 1940.
Yoshinobu Kimoto is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He served at Yonezawa Women's Junior College from circa 1986 to 1994 and at Koshien Junior College from circa 1994 to 2001.

Yoshinori Takeuchi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1933 to 1936 and later served there as a professor from circa 1959 to 1977.

Yoshio Kawakatsu was a sinology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1957–1960), and served on the faculty at Kyoto University from circa 1952 to 1984.

Yoshiro Imaeda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, the EPHE under Bernard Frank and Ariane Macdonald, and held a research post at the CNRS from circa 1974 to 2012.

Yoshiro Tamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1949). He held posts at Toyo University, Komazawa University, Rissho University, the University of Tokyo (~1964–1982), and the University of Chicago (1985).

Yoshitaka Iriya was a sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1961–1968), Kyoto University (attested 1967–1969), Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–1981), and Hanazono University (~1981–1991).

Yoshitsugu Sawai is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under scholars including Daniel H. H. Ingalls and John B. Carman, and held a professorship at Tenri University from circa 1986 to 2017.
Yoshiyasu Yonezawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held research and lecturer positions at Taisho University, attested between 1998 and 2015.
Yoshiyuki Kawazoe studied at Tohoku University from circa 1966 to 1975 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1975 to 2012.
Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939). He spent his career at Rissho University, serving as professor (~1957–1987) and director (~1980–1987).

Youru Wang works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After earning a PhD at Temple University, he held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 1999) and Rowan University (attested 2003–2007).

Yozo Taniyama works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1996) and held posts at Sophia University, St. Thomas University, Shitennoji University, and Tohoku University (~2012).
Yu Yan Pang completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, as well as teacher Eric Kvan. Pang's work is situated in Buddhist studies.
Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar. Tsui pursued master's studies at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu, studied under Natasha Heller and Sheng Yen.

Yu-kwan Ng specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and McMaster University, he studied under Zongsan Mou, Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara, and held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University and National Central University.
Yu-min Lee specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Lee studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington and served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).
